title: Microsoft Dataverse: Python SDK for scripting and agent workflows
summary: The summary says that no SDK switch exists in the admin centres, but the research establishes only that Microsoft has not documented one. Narrow that assertion to the documented gap; the roadmap facts and the listed control paths and calls are supported.

claims.claim: The SDK lets Python developers read and write Dataverse data.
claims.quote: The Dataverse SDK for Python enables Python developers to interact directly with Microsoft Dataverse. You can easily access, manage, and manipulate data stored in Dataverse by using familiar Python syntax.

claims.claim: Using the SDK does not require .NET knowledge.
claims.quote: You don't need any .NET knowledge.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The SDK is published under open-source licensing.
claims.quote: The SDK for Python is published under open-source licensing.

claims.claim: Developers install the SDK package from PyPI using pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client.
claims.quote:
This command installs the latest stable release of the SDK from a pypi.org package.

pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client

claims.claim: Learn also documents installing the SDK from its GitHub source repository.
claims.quote: Run the following command to install the SDK from the project's GitHub source instead of from the package. Install the client from the PyPi package or from the source, but not both.

claims.claim: The getting-started page requires Python 3.10+.
claims.quote: An activated Python 3.10+ environment.

claims.claim: The reference-architecture page instead lists Python 3.13 or later.
claims.quote:
Prerequisites

- Access to a Power Platform environment with Dataverse
- Appropriate security roles
- Python 3.13 or later
- Network access to PyPI for SDK installation

claims.claim: The getting-started prerequisites include OAuth authentication configured for the application.
claims.quote: OAuth authentication configured for your application.

claims.claim: The getting-started prerequisites include network access to PyPI.
claims.quote: Network access to https://pypi.org to obtain the SDK packages.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Authentication uses the Azure Identity credential supplied to the SDK.
claims.quote: The SDK client requires any Azure Identity TokenCredential implementation for OAuth authentication with Dataverse.

claims.claim: The SDK calls the Dataverse Web API internally rather than adding a separate data store.
claims.quote: The SDK provides a Python programming interface that internally calls the Dataverse Web API.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; summary; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SDK data operations use existing Dataverse security roles, not a separate SDK permission model.
claims.quote: Role-based access control: Enforces Dataverse security roles and policies for all data operations.

claims.claim: Customising a table or its columns requires appropriate customisation privileges.
claims.quote: Creating a column is a metadata change: you need privileges to customize the table, and the new column becomes a permanent part of your environment's schema.

claims.claim: The overview lists create, retrieve, update and delete data operations.
claims.quote: CRUD operations | Support for create, retrieve, update, and delete data operations by using a single request.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Bulk operations use CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple and BulkDelete to operate on multiple records in a call.
claims.quote: Specify multiple operations in a single web service call. This feature uses Dataverse's native CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple, and BulkDelete Web API operations

claims.claim: The SDK supports read-only direct SQL SELECT queries.
claims.quote: Direct-SQL queries | Supports simple read-only "SELECT" statements with paging.

claims.claim: The SDK provides pandas DataFrame wrappers for CRUD operations.
claims.quote: Client wrappers are provided for all CRUD operations where DataFrames and Series data types are returned to the caller.

claims.claim: The SDK uploads files to Dataverse file columns.
claims.quote: File operations | Upload files to a Dataverse file column with automatic chunking for large files.

claims.claim: The SDK supports batch requests.
claims.quote: Batch operations | Send multiple CRUD, table metadata, and SQL query operations in a single HTTP request with optional transactional changesets.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The SDK supports creating, updating and deleting custom tables and columns.
claims.quote: The SDK supports create, update, and delete (CUD) of custom tables and columns, optional solution association, plus retrieve and list table definitions.

claims.claim: The overview lists structured error handling.
claims.quote: Error handling: structured exception hierarchy with detailed error context and retry guidance.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Opt-in HTTP diagnostics logging writes all HTTP requests and responses to a file.
claims.quote: HTTP diagnostics logging: opt-in file-based logging of all HTTP requests and responses

claims.claim: HTTP diagnostics logging automatically redacts sensitive headers such as authorization.
claims.quote: with automatic redaction of sensitive headers, such as authorization.

claims.claim: The overview feature list does not name autonomous data agents, form prediction, autofill, MCP or A2A.
claims.quote: Searched: overview feature list for autonomous data agents, form prediction, autofill, MCP and A2A; opened and read learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/sdk-python/overview in full. None is named in that list.

claims.claim: SDK workflows can extract tables into pandas DataFrames for analysis.
claims.quote: Extract and transform: Load tables into Pandas DataFrames for cleaning, feature engineering, and exploratory analysis.

claims.claim: After extraction into a notebook or file, the extracted data is outside Dataverse's security boundary.
claims.quote: However, after the data has been extracted it is no longer protected by the security boundary provided by Dynamics 365 (online) and is instead controlled directly by the customer.

claims.claim: The getting-started example identifies InteractiveBrowserCredential and AzureCliCredential as development options.
claims.quote:
# Development options
credential = InteractiveBrowserCredential()  # Browser authentication
# credential = AzureCliCredential()          # If logged in via 'az login'

claims.claim: The getting-started example identifies ClientSecretCredential and CertificateCredential as production options.
claims.quote:
# Production options
# credential = ClientSecretCredential(tenant_id, client_id, client_secret)
# credential = CertificateCredential(tenant_id, client_id, cert_path)

claims.claim: InteractiveBrowserCredential accepts a client_id and otherwise authenticates to an Azure development application.
claims.quote: client_id ... Client ID of the Microsoft Entra application that users will sign into. ... If not specified, users will authenticate to an Azure development application, which is not recommended for production scenarios.

claims.claim: Application users associate registered applications with environment access and assigned security roles.
claims.quote: This application user is given access to your environment's data on behalf of the user who's using your application. ... Select the edit icon to select security roles for the new application user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[0].governs; Governance controls
claims.claim: App access control is a general environment control that allows or blocks client app IDs, with applicability depending on authentication context.
claims.quote: Dataverse authentication validates the client app ID in the user's token against a list of allowed and blocked apps configured for the environment.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: App access control requires a managed environment.
claims.quote:
Verify that your environment is a managed environment

Your environment must be a managed environment.

claims.claim: The app access control prerequisites name the Power Platform admin and Dynamics 365 admin roles.
claims.quote:
Verify your role

There are two Power Platform related service admin roles you can assign to provide a high level of admin management:

- Power Platform admin
- Dynamics 365 admin

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: App access control does not apply to partner apps making service-to-service calls.
claims.quote: Client app access control isn't applied to the following apps: ... Partner apps with service-to-service calls

claims.claim: Microsoft points to deactivating or deleting application users to block partner apps making service-to-service calls.
claims.quote:
Partner apps with service-to-service calls

To block these apps, make them inactive or delete them from the environment in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: client.files.upload automatically creates a missing file column.
claims.quote:
client.files.upload(
    "account",
    account_id,
    "new_Document",
    "/path/to/document.pdf",
)

Important

If the file column doesn't exist, the SDK creates it automatically.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An automatically created file column is a permanent schema change.
claims.quote: the new column becomes a permanent part of your environment's schema.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn advises creating file columns in advance in production.
claims.quote: In production environments, create file columns in advance rather than relying on automatic creation.

claims.claim: After package installation, dataverse-install-claude-skill optionally installs two Claude skills.
claims.quote:
you can optionally install two Claude Skills when installing the SDK from a package.

pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client && dataverse-install-claude-skill

claims.claim: The installed Claude skill definitions reside on the developer's computer.
claims.quote: you can find skill definitions in the .claude/skills/dataverse-sdk-use/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/dataverse-sdk-dev/SKILL.md files on your development computer.

claims.claim: The SDK automatically retries temporary failures such as API throttling.
claims.quote: Automatic retries | Handle networking problems that might occur for operations that fail due to temporary problems, such as API throttling or service unavailability.

claims.claim: Dataverse service protection limits apply to external web service requests.
claims.quote: Service protection limits apply to all external web service requests, not only the CRUD operations on tables counted against entitlement limits.

claims.claim: Service protection limits include limits per user account, supporting the warning about callers sharing an account.
claims.quote: We limit the number of concurrent connections per user account, the number of API requests per connection, and the amount of execution time that can be used for each connection.

claims.claim: Dataverse CRUD, assign and share operations count toward request limits from any client or application using SOAP or REST, including SDK Web API traffic.
claims.quote: All create, read, update, and delete (CRUD), assign, and share operations ... These operations can be from any client or application (including Dynamics 365) and use any endpoint (SOAP or REST).

claims.claim: Application, non-interactive, administrative and SYSTEM identities share tenant-level non-licensed request limits.
claims.quote:
These limits are defined and pooled at the tenant level. ... These identities include:

- Application users
- Non-interactive users
- Administrative users
- SYSTEM user

claims.claim: No SDK-specific meter or charge is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse SDK for Python" "meter" "charge"; Dataverse SDK Python licensing user application license API access pricing meter. Read SDK overview/get-started, Power Platform request allocations, API limits and storage capacity; no SDK-specific charge found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The getting-started prerequisites name read/write access to a Dataverse environment but no Microsoft licence.
claims.quote: Read/write access to a Dataverse environment. ... OAuth authentication configured for your application. ... An activated Python 3.10+ environment. ... Pandas version 2.0.0+. ... Network access to https://pypi.org to obtain the SDK packages.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The SDK pages do not publish a Microsoft user or application licence requirement specific to SDK traffic, so the briefing reports its licensing model as unknown rather than free.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse SDK Python licensing user application license API access pricing meter; Dataverse API licensing direct access external application users. Read SDK overview/get-started, architecture, application users and request allocations. No SDK-specific Microsoft SKU found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Using the SDK is user-opt-in: a developer chooses to install and run it, while the roadmap separately calls the item automatically enabled.
claims.quote:
From a terminal window, run the following command. This command installs the latest stable release of the SDK from a pypi.org package.

pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client

claims.claim: App access control is at Power Platform admin center > Security > Identity and access > App access control > environment > Set up app access control > Access control.
claims.quote: select Security. ... select Identity and access. ... select App access control ... Select the environment ... Select the Set up app access control button. ... Access control dropdown list.

claims.claim: pac env list-settings --environment <environment-url> --filter application reads matching organization settings and does not change access control.
claims.quote:
pac env list-settings

List environment settings ... --environment ... The value may be a Guid or absolute https URL. ... --filter ... Show only settings containing filter criteria ... this command returns all the columns

claims.claim: New application users are created at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user.
claims.quote: Select Manage ... select Environments. Then select an environment. ... Select Settings. ... Select Users + permissions, and then select Application users. ... Select + New app user

claims.claim: The documented addAppUser POST endpoint uses api-version=2020-10-01 and the servicePrincipalAppId request-body key.
The application-user API documentation is marked preview.
claims.quote:
Create a Dataverse application user (preview)

[This article is pre-release documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The addAppUser API always adds the application user as System Administrator.
claims.quote: This always adds the application user as a System Administrator.

claims.claim: Environment auditing is at Power Platform admin center > Security > Compliance > Auditing > environment > Set up auditing > Turn on auditing.
claims.quote: select Security > Compliance. ... Select the Auditing tile. ... Select the environment ... Select Set up auditing. In the Auditing pane, select Turn on auditing.

claims.claim: GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations with the four listed $select properties retrieves auditing settings.
claims.quote:
Retrieve organization settings

Use the following queries to retrieve your organization settings.

GET [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations?$select=
auditsettings,
isauditenabled,
auditretentionperiodv2,
isuseraccessauditenabled,
useraccessauditinginterval HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: System Administrator or System Customizer can enable auditing.
claims.quote: You must have a system administrator or system customizer role or equivalent permissions to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Recording scripted data changes requires auditing at environment, table and column levels.
claims.quote: Dataverse auditing also logs user access through an app or through the SDK in an environment. ... First, turn on auditing at the environment level. To log data changes in a table, turn on auditing for the table and for the column.

claims.claim: User-access logging requires the separate Log access setting as well as environment auditing.
claims.quote: To turn on user access auditing (log access) or activity logging (Read logs), turn on auditing at the environment level. ... Log access | Log whenever the system is accessed, generally by signing in.

claims.where: controls[3]; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no tenant or environment UI or API setting specific to allowing or blocking the Python SDK as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse SDK for Python" "switch"; "Dataverse SDK for Python" "admin" "enable"; SDK tenant environment setting Power Platform API PowerShell pac. Read SDK overview/get-started, app access control and pac env; no SDK switch found.

claims.claim: There is no SDK switch in the admin centres.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse SDK for Python" "switch"; "Dataverse SDK for Python" "admin" "enable"; SDK tenant environment setting Power Platform API PowerShell pac. Read SDK overview/get-started and app access control. No source states that no SDK switch exists.
claims.fix: Replace 'there is no SDK switch in the admin centres' with 'Microsoft Learn documents no SDK-specific switch at the time of writing (November 2026)'. The search supports an undocumented control, not a categorical assertion that none exists.

claims.claim: App access control has an audit mode for reviewing apps before enforcing restrictions.
claims.quote: In audit mode, you must select at least one application to allow access. However, app access control isn't enforced in audit mode. You get a list of apps accessing the environment whether or not they're allowed or denied access.

claims.claim: App access control has an enabled mode that enforces allowed and blocked app access.
claims.quote:
Turn on enabled mode

Start blocking apps that are blocked and allow only approved apps. You can select apps to either have Allowed or Blocked access.

claims.claim: The app access audit log can be filtered for ApplicationBasedAccessDenied events.
claims.quote: Select the dropdown arrow near the Event heading, then find and select ApplicationBasedAccessDenied and ApplicationBasedAccessAllowed.

claims.claim: The app access audit log can be filtered for ApplicationBasedAccessAllowed events.
claims.quote: Select the dropdown arrow near the Event heading, then find and select ApplicationBasedAccessDenied and ApplicationBasedAccessAllowed.

claims.claim: Human security-role assignment is under the environment's Users + permissions settings.
claims.quote: Add users to a security role ... Select Settings ... Select Users + permissions > Security roles. ... Select a security role ... Select Members ... select the + Add people.

claims.claim: Writing rows or files consumes Dataverse storage capacity.
claims.quote: All Dataverse tables, including system tables, are included in the storage capacity reports. Files such as .pdf (or any other file attachment type) are stored in file storage. However, the database stores certain attributes needed to access the files.
